description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and accuracy, labeled as "ACC (%)", for six different models or methods. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and employs a linear scale ranging from 60 to above 80, with major tick marks spaced at intervals of 5 units. The plot contains six solid lines, each corresponding to a legend entry and plotted across four discrete x-axis data points located approximately at 3, 30, 300, and 3000. All lines exhibit a steady upward trend from left to right. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 64% and rising to end at roughly 71%. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at about 65.5% and increasing to approximately 73%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting near 67.5% and concluding at about 75.2%. A purple line with pentagon markers corresponds to a legend entry obscured by a gray rectangle; it starts at about 69.5% and rises to approximately 77.5%. The "MEND" method is illustrated with a brown line and diamond markers, initiating at approximately 70.8% and reaching roughly 80.2% at the final point. Finally, the "ROME" method is represented by a green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 74.2% and increasing to end at roughly 84.5%. Both axes feature a light dashed grid to aid in reading values.
